# URL Shortener (greenfield-a37c3044)

Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 URL shortener. Write path creates base62 short codes from a batched Redis counter (`INCRBY 1000`) with a Postgres-sequence fallback; read path serves `302` redirects from a Redis read-through cache in front of Postgres (source of truth, Flyway-migrated). Read and write surfaces are independently deployable via Spring profiles.

Authentication and analytics are explicitly out of scope.

## Contents

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/main/java/com/example/shortener/write` | `POST /api/v1/urls` controller + service (`@Profile("!read")`) |
| `src/main/java/com/example/shortener/read` | `GET /{short_code}` controller, cache, read service (`@Profile("!write")`) |
| `src/main/java/com/example/shortener/codegen` | Base62 codec, Redis batch counter, DB-sequence fallback, allocator |
| `src/main/java/com/example/shortener/domain` | `UrlMapping` entity, `CodeSource`, repository |
| `src/main/java/com/example/shortener/api` | DTOs + `GlobalExceptionHandler` (problem+json) |
| `src/main/resources/db/migration` | Flyway forward-only migrations (`V1__create_urls_table.sql`) |
| `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` | Committed API contract (verified by `OpenApiContractIT`) |
| `docs/operations.md` | Degradation behaviour, counter gaps |

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| JDK | 25 |
| Maven | via provisioned `./mvnw` |
| Docker | required only for integration tests (Testcontainers) and container runs |
| Postgres | 17.x (runtime) |
| Redis | 7.x (runtime, optional — service degrades without it) |

## Setup

```bash
git clone <repo> && cd <repo>
./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile
```

Local backing services (example):

```bash
docker run -d --name pg   -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=shortener postgres:17
docker run -d --name redis -p 6379:6379 redis:7
```

Flyway runs automatically on application start and creates the `urls` table and the `url_code_seq` sequence.

## Run

```bash
# combined (default profile): both read and write endpoints
./mvnw spring-boot:run

# write-only instance
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=write ./mvnw spring-boot:run

# read-only instance
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=read  ./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

Docker:

```bash
docker build -t url-shortener:local .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 \
  -e SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=read \
  -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host.docker.internal:5432/shortener \
  -e SPRING_DATA_REDIS_HOST=host.docker.internal \
  -e SHORTENER_BASE_URL=https://sho.rt \
  url-shortener:local
```

The image is a multi-stage build (JDK 25 build stage, slim JRE runtime) and runs as a non-root user on port 8080.

### Profile matrix

| Profile | `POST /api/v1/urls` | `GET /{short_code}` |
|---|---|---|
| default (none) | 201 | 302 |
| `write` | 201 | 404 |
| `read` | 404 | 302 |

Controllers are registered conditionally; an absent controller yields `404` from the global handler as problem+json.

## Configuration

| Property | Env | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shortener.base-url` | `SHORTENER_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Prefix of the returned `short_url` |
| `shortener.counter.batch-size` | `SHORTENER_COUNTER_BATCHSIZE` | `1000` | Redis `INCRBY` reservation size |
| `shortener.counter.seed-offset` | `SHORTENER_COUNTER_SEEDOFFSET` | `238328` (62^3) | Guarantees generated codes ≥ 3 chars |
| `shortener.cache.default-ttl` | `SHORTENER_CACHE_DEFAULTTTL` | `24h` | TTL when no `expiration_date` (AMB-9 default) |
| `shortener.cache.key-prefix` | `SHORTENER_CACHE_KEYPREFIX` | `shortener:url:` | Redis key prefix |
| `spring.datasource.url` | `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` | local | Postgres JDBC URL |
| `spring.data.redis.host` / `.port` | `SPRING_DATA_REDIS_HOST` / `_PORT` | `localhost` / `6379` | Cache + counter |

Redis keys used: `shortener:counter` (global counter), `shortener:url:{short_code}` (cache entries).

## Test

```bash
./mvnw -q test                      # unit tests only, no Docker required
./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test  # layering / cycle rules
./mvnw -q -Pit verify               # Testcontainers ITs (Postgres + Redis) + OpenAPI parity
./mvnw -q spotless:check            # formatting (advisory)
```

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| `CreateShortUrlIT` | 201 payload + persisted row, 400 with no row, 409 alias conflict, no dedup |
| `RedirectIT` | 302 + `Location` + `Cache-Control: private`, 404, 410, problem+json |
| `CacheAndFallbackIT` | Cache hit serves redirect, TTL ≤ remaining expiry, Redis-down write → `db_sequence`, Redis-down read → Postgres |
| `ProfileSeparationIT` | read/write/default profile endpoint registration |
| `OpenApiContractIT` | Committed `openapi.yaml` vs springdoc dump, per operation and status code |

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs compile → spotless (advisory) → ArchitectureTest → unit → `-Pit verify`.

## API summary

Contract: `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1). All errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) emitted by a single `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### `POST /api/v1/urls` — createShortUrl

Request (snake_case):

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `long_url` | string, required | `http`/`https` only, 1–2048 chars |
| `custom_alias` | string, optional | `^[0-9a-zA-Z]{3,32}$` |
| `expiration_date` | ISO-8601 date-time, optional | must be in the future |

Responses:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 201 | `{short_url, short_code, long_url, expires_at, code_source}`; row persisted, `created_by` null |
| 400 | Validation failure (scheme, length, alias charset/length, malformed/past expiry, unreadable body); nothing persisted |
| 409 | `custom_alias` already taken; existing mapping unchanged |
| 500 | Unhandled error, rendered as problem+json |

Re-posting an already-shortened `long_url` without an alias always returns a **new distinct code** (no deduplication).

```bash
curl -sS -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/urls \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"long_url":"https://example.com/some/path","expiration_date":"2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
# 201 {"short_url":"http://localhost:8080/aB3x9","short_code":"aB3x9",...,"code_source":"redis"}
```

### `GET /{short_code}` — redirectToLongUrl

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 302 | `Location: <long_url>`, `Cache-Control: private` |
| 404 | Unknown code (cache and DB miss) |
| 410 | Code exists but `expires_at` is in the past |
| 500 | Unhandled error, problem+json |

```bash
curl -i localhost:8080/aB3x9
```

## Data model

`urls`: `short_code varchar(32) PK`, `long_url varchar(2048) NOT NULL`, `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL`, `expires_at timestamptz NULL`, `created_by varchar(255) NULL` (always NULL in this release), `code_source varchar(16) NOT NULL` (`redis` | `db_sequence`), plus partial index on `expires_at` and CHECK constraints on format/length/source.

`url_code_seq`: Postgres sequence starting at 238328, used only as the Redis-outage fallback counter.

Migrations are forward-only; future changes follow expand/contract (never edit `V1`).

## Behaviour notes

- **Code generation**: each write instance reserves 1000 counter values with one Redis `INCRBY`; values are offset by the seed and base62-encoded. `code_source=redis`.
- **Redis outage (write)**: allocator logs a degradation warning and uses `nextval('url_code_seq')`; response is still 201 with `code_source=db_sequence`.
- **Redis outage (read)**: cache get/put failures are swallowed and logged; redirects are served from Postgres.
- **Counter gaps**: unused values in a reserved batch are discarded on restart (accepted, AMB-10).

## Open ambiguities (implemented at documented defaults, pending confirmation)

| ID | Question | Applied default |
|---|---|---|
| AMB-9 | Cache TTL when no expiration | Fixed configurable 24h |
| AMB-10 | Gaps on restart acceptable? | Yes, gaps accepted |
| AMB-11 | Minimum length for generated codes | Counter seeded at 62^3 so codes ≥ 3 chars |

## Out of scope

Authentication/authorization, analytics and click tracking, populating `created_by`, link editing/deletion, custom short-domain management.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. Format based on Keep a Changelog; versioning is semantic.

## [1.0.0] - Run greenfield-a37c3044 (spec v2)

### Added
- `POST /api/v1/urls` (createShortUrl): creates a short code from a long URL with optional `custom_alias` and `expiration_date`; returns 201 with `short_url`, `short_code`, `long_url`, `expires_at`, `code_source` (US-1, AC-1/AC-4).
- `GET /{short_code}` (redirectToLongUrl): 302 redirect with `Location` and `Cache-Control: private` (US-2, AC-7).
- Base62 short-code generation from a globally unique Redis counter reserved in batches of 1000 via `INCRBY`, seeded at 62^3 so codes are at least 3 characters (US-3, AC-10).
- Postgres sequence fallback (`url_code_seq`) when Redis is unavailable during allocation; persisted as `code_source='db_sequence'` (AC-11).
- Redis read-through cache `shortener:url:{short_code}` with TTL = min(remaining time to `expires_at`, 24h default); cache hits skip Postgres entirely (US-4, AC-12).
- Graceful cache bypass with logged degradation when Redis is unreachable on the read path (AC-13).
- Independently deployable read/write surfaces via Spring profiles `read`, `write` and the combined default (US-5, AC-14).
- Global `@RestControllerAdvice` emitting RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` for 400, 404, 409, 410 and unhandled 500 (US-6, AC-16).
- Flyway migration `V1__create_urls_table.sql`: `urls` table (`short_code` PK, `long_url`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `created_by` nullable, `code_source`), partial index on `expires_at`, CHECK constraints, and `url_code_seq`.
- Committed OpenAPI 3.1 document `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml`, verified against the springdoc dump by `OpenApiContractIT`.
- Unit tests (validation, base62 codec, allocator fallback, counter concurrency, cache TTL, controllers) and Testcontainers integration tests for Postgres and Redis (AC-15).
- Multi-stage non-root `Dockerfile`, GitHub Actions CI workflow, `README.md` and `docs/operations.md`.

### Validation
- Gates passed: scope, compile, style (advisory), security, architecture, unit, integration, contract, acceptance (advisory).

### Notes / Known limitations
- Authentication, authorization, analytics and click tracking are out of scope; `created_by` is nullable and always NULL.
- Identical long URLs are never deduplicated; each request yields a new short code.
- Unused values of a reserved 1000-value counter batch are discarded on restart, producing gaps in code space.
- Ambiguities AMB-9 (24h default cache TTL), AMB-10 (gaps accepted), AMB-11 (counter seeded for ≥3-char codes) are implemented at their documented defaults and await confirmation.

# ADR-001: Base62 codes from a batched Redis counter

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Short codes must be globally unique across concurrently running write instances and stay short.
- **Decision**: Reserve 1000 counter values per instance with a single `INCRBY` on `shortener:counter`, hand them out locally and base62-encode them.
- **Rejected alternative**: UUID or random-with-collision-retry — requires a uniqueness read per attempt and yields longer codes.
- **Consequence**: One Redis round-trip per 1000 creations; uniqueness is structural, not probabilistic; codes are non-sequential-looking but enumerable.

# ADR-002: Postgres sequence fallback on Redis outage

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Redis is a single dependency of the write path; an outage must not stop link creation.
- **Decision**: On Redis failure, allocate from `nextval('url_code_seq')` and persist `code_source='db_sequence'`.
- **Rejected alternative**: Fail the write with 503 — availability of link creation outweighs counter-space contiguity.
- **Consequence**: Codes remain unique (disjoint seeded ranges are not guaranteed contiguous); `code_source` makes degraded writes auditable.

# ADR-003: Discard unused counter batch on restart

- **Status**: Accepted (AMB-10 default, pending confirmation)
- **Context**: An instance holding a reserved 1000-value range loses the remainder when it restarts.
- **Decision**: Accept gaps; never persist or reclaim reserved ranges.
- **Rejected alternative**: Persist and reclaim ranges — reintroduces the shared-state write that batching was meant to remove.
- **Consequence**: Code space is consumed faster than links are created; no correctness impact; documented in `docs/operations.md`.

# ADR-004: Counter seeded at 62^3

- **Status**: Accepted (AMB-11 default, pending confirmation)
- **Context**: Custom aliases must be 3–32 chars; raw counter values would produce 1–2 char generated codes initially.
- **Decision**: Offset every counter value by 238328 so generated base62 codes are at least 3 characters.
- **Rejected alternative**: Allow 1–2 character generated codes — would split the code format from the alias rule and complicate validation.
- **Consequence**: One uniform `^[0-9a-zA-Z]{3,32}$` code format; ~238k short codes are never issued.

# ADR-005: Cache TTL bounded by remaining expiry

- **Status**: Accepted (AMB-9 default, pending confirmation)
- **Context**: Cached mappings must never outlive the link they point to.
- **Decision**: TTL = min(remaining time to `expires_at`, configurable default 24h when no expiry).
- **Rejected alternative**: Cache indefinitely — a stale entry could serve a redirect for an expired link.
- **Consequence**: Bounded staleness; expired links reliably return 410; a small steady cache-miss rate against Postgres.

# ADR-006: Redis is cache only, Postgres is the source of truth

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Mappings must survive a full Redis flush or outage.
- **Decision**: Redis holds only derived state (counter + cache entries); all mappings are written to Postgres synchronously.
- **Rejected alternative**: Write-behind or Redis-primary storage — durability of mappings is non-negotiable.
- **Consequence**: Redis can be flushed at any time with no data loss; write latency includes a Postgres commit.

# ADR-007: Profile-gated read/write surfaces in one artifact

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Redirect traffic must scale independently of link creation.
- **Decision**: One deployable jar; `@Profile("!write")` on the redirect controller and `@Profile("!read")` on the write controller; profiles `read`, `write`, default.
- **Rejected alternative**: Two Maven modules/services — shared schema and DTOs do not justify the build and deployment overhead yet.
- **Consequence**: A read instance answers 404 to POST and vice versa; one image, three deployment shapes.

# ADR-008: Single problem+json exception handler

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Every non-2xx response must have one consistent, contract-documented shape.
- **Decision**: One `@RestControllerAdvice` extending `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler` maps all errors to RFC 9457 `ProblemDetail` with `application/problem+json`.
- **Rejected alternative**: Per-controller `ResponseEntity` error bodies — the shape would drift from the committed contract.
- **Consequence**: Controllers never build error bodies; no stack traces or internal identifiers leak to clients.

# ADR-009: Versioned write path, unversioned redirect path

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The API needs a version prefix, but short links must stay short.
- **Decision**: Write endpoint is `/api/v1/urls`; redirects stay at the bare root `/{short_code}`.
- **Rejected alternative**: Version the redirect path too — every extra path segment lengthens every shared link.
- **Consequence**: Root path is reserved for short codes; future root-level routes must not collide with the code charset.

# ADR-010: Forward-only Flyway migrations with expand/contract

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Schema changes must be reviewable and deterministic across environments.
- **Decision**: Versioned Flyway scripts under `db/migration`; every future change is a new `Vn` file following expand then contract.
- **Rejected alternative**: Hibernate `ddl-auto=update` — unreviewable and non-deterministic between environments.
- **Consequence**: `V1` is immutable once integration tests have run; no destructive change may ship inside a single release.

# ADR-011: `code_source` as varchar + CHECK, not a Postgres ENUM

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: A third code source (e.g. snowflake IDs) is plausible later.
- **Decision**: Store `code_source` as `varchar(16)` with `CHECK (code_source IN ('redis','db_sequence'))`.
- **Rejected alternative**: Postgres ENUM type — adding a value later requires a type migration.
- **Consequence**: Adding a source is an `ALTER ... CHECK` constraint change; type safety lives in the Java `CodeSource` enum.

# ADR-012: No outbox and no event topics in this release

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Analytics and click tracking are explicit non-goals; no domain events exist.
- **Decision**: Ship no Kafka topics and no outbox table.
- **Rejected alternative**: Pre-emptively add an outbox table — dead schema unverifiable by any acceptance criterion.
- **Consequence**: When analytics arrives, an outbox (`aggregate_id`, `event_type`, `payload jsonb`, …) plus `.v1`-suffixed event schemas is added by an expand migration.

# ADR-013: Blocking Spring MVC, not WebFlux

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The redirect path is latency-sensitive; persistence uses JPA and Flyway.
- **Decision**: Use the servlet stack (Spring MVC) with blocking JPA/Redis clients.
- **Rejected alternative**: WebFlux — JPA and Flyway are blocking, and redirect latency is dominated by one cache lookup.
- **Consequence**: Simpler code and testing; horizontal scaling of read instances is the throughput lever.

# ADR-014: Alias conflict detected by pre-check plus PK violation

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Two concurrent requests may claim the same custom alias.
- **Decision**: Pre-check `existsByShortCode`, then catch `DataIntegrityViolationException` on the primary key and map both to 409.
- **Rejected alternative**: Pre-check alone — races under concurrent creation of the same alias.
- **Consequence**: 409 is correct under concurrency; the existing mapping is never overwritten; one extra read per aliased write.

# ADR-015: Testcontainers for integration tests

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Sequences, TTL semantics and Redis failure behaviour must be exercised realistically.
- **Decision**: `*IT` classes under the `it` Maven profile start real Postgres and Redis containers via Testcontainers.
- **Rejected alternative**: H2 plus embedded Redis — diverges from production behaviour for sequences and TTLs.
- **Consequence**: `./mvnw test` stays container-free and fast; `-Pit verify` requires Docker and runs ~2 minutes.

# ADR-016: Committed OpenAPI verified by a parity test

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: A handwritten contract drifts silently from the implementation.
- **Decision**: Commit `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` and have `OpenApiContractIT` diff it against the springdoc dump operation- and status-code-wise.
- **Rejected alternative**: Hand-maintain the document with no parity test — the contract gate would pass on stale documents.
- **Consequence**: Any endpoint or status-code change fails the build until the committed document is updated.

# ADR-017: `created_by` kept nullable and unpopulated

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Authentication is out of scope, but ownership will be needed later.
- **Decision**: Ship the nullable `created_by varchar(255)` column and never write to it in this release.
- **Rejected alternative**: Omit the column and add it later — costs an extra expand/contract cycle.
- **Consequence**: No PII is stored today; when auth lands, the column is backfilled and then made NOT NULL via expand/contract.

# Runbook — URL Shortener (greenfield-a37c3044)

## 1. Service topology

| Deployment | Profile | Endpoints | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| write | `write` | `POST /api/v1/urls` | Postgres (RW), Redis counter (optional) |
| read | `read` | `GET /{short_code}` | Postgres (RO), Redis cache (optional) |
| combined | default | both | Postgres, Redis |

Postgres is the source of truth. Redis holds only derived state (`shortener:counter`, `shortener:url:*`) and may be flushed at any time without data loss.

## 2. Health checks

| Check | Command | Healthy |
|---|---|---|
| Liveness | `GET /actuator/health/liveness` | 200 `UP` |
| Readiness | `GET /actuator/health/readiness` | 200 `UP` (DB reachable) |
| Write smoke | `curl -sS -XPOST $BASE/api/v1/urls -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"long_url":"https://example.com/health"}'` | 201, body has `short_code`, `code_source` |
| Read smoke | `curl -i $BASE/<code-from-above>` | 302, `Location`, `Cache-Control: private` |
| Error contract | `curl -i -XPOST $BASE/api/v1/urls -d '{"long_url":"ftp://x"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'` | 400 `application/problem+json` |
| Contract drift | `./mvnw -q -Pit verify` (CI) | `OpenApiContractIT` green |

Redis is intentionally **not** part of readiness: the service is designed to serve traffic without it.

## 3. Dashboards / signals to watch

| Signal | Source | Normal | Alert |
|---|---|---|---|
| Redirect p99 latency | HTTP server metrics, `GET /{short_code}` | < 50 ms | > 200 ms 5 min |
| Redirect status mix | 302 / 404 / 410 ratio | 404+410 < 5% | 404 spike (bad links or wrong DB) |
| Create success rate | `POST /api/v1/urls` 2xx ratio | > 99% | < 95% 5 min |
| `code_source=db_sequence` rate | write logs / response field | 0 | any sustained non-zero = Redis degraded |
| Cache hit ratio | `RedisUrlCache` hit/miss logs or counters | > 90% steady state | < 50% (cold cache or Redis down) |
| Cache degradation warnings | log pattern `cache degradation` | 0/min | > 0 sustained |
| Allocator fallback warnings | log pattern `falling back to db_sequence` | 0/min | > 0 sustained |
| Postgres connections / pool saturation | Hikari metrics | < 70% | > 90% |
| 5xx rate | HTTP server metrics | ~0 | > 0.1% |
| Flyway state | startup logs | `Successfully applied`/`up to date` | `Migration ... failed` or checksum mismatch |

## 4. Degraded modes

| Mode | Symptom | Client impact | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Redis down — write path | Warn `Primary short-code counter (redis) unavailable ...; falling back to db_sequence`; responses carry `code_source=db_sequence` | None (201 still returned) | Restore Redis; no data repair needed. Watch Postgres sequence load |
| Redis down — read path | Cache degradation warnings; every redirect hits Postgres | Higher redirect latency; possible DB saturation | Restore Redis; if DB saturates, scale read replicas/pool or shed traffic |
| Redis flushed | Cache hit ratio → 0, counter restarts from 0 | Latency spike; **no duplicate codes** (seed offset + PK CHECK + 409 on conflict) | Verify 500 rate stays flat; if PK collisions appear, re-seed `shortener:counter` above the current max encoded value |
| Postgres unavailable | Readiness DOWN; 500 problem+json on both paths | Full outage of writes; reads fail on cache miss | Failover/restore Postgres. Cached codes keep redirecting until TTL |
| Postgres read-only/failover | Writes 500, reads OK | Creation unavailable | Scale down/disable write instances until primary is back |
| High 410 rate | Many expired links | Expected for time-boxed campaigns | No action unless unexpected — check clock skew on instances |
| Clock skew | Wrong 410s, wrong TTLs | Premature expiry | Verify NTP on all instances and DB |

Accepted behaviours (not incidents): gaps in the code sequence after instance restarts (ADR-003); duplicate short codes for the same long URL (no deduplication by design).

## 5. Common operations

```bash
# Inspect a mapping
psql -c "select short_code, long_url, created_at, expires_at, code_source from urls where short_code='aB3x9';"

# Inspect / evict a cache entry
redis-cli GET  shortener:url:aB3x9
redis-cli TTL  shortener:url:aB3x9
redis-cli DEL  shortener:url:aB3x9

# Counter state
redis-cli GET shortener:counter
psql -c "select last_value from url_code_seq;"

# Re-seed the Redis counter after a flush (X = safe high-water mark)
redis-cli SET shortener:counter <X>
```

## 6. Rollback

| Scope | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Application (bad release) | Redeploy the previous image tag per surface (`read`, `write`) — the app is stateless. Roll back read instances first, then write |
| Schema | `V1` is the only migration; it is additive. Flyway is forward-only — **never** hand-edit or delete an applied migration. A defective future `Vn` is undone with a new compensating `Vn+1` |
| Config change | Revert the env var / property and restart the affected instances; no data migration required |
| Redis state | Safe to `FLUSHDB` for the shortener keyspace; re-seed `shortener:counter` (see §5) before restoring write traffic |
| Emergency write stop | Scale write instances to zero or flip them to the `read` profile — POST then returns 404; redirects are unaffected |

Rollback verification: run the write and read smoke checks (§2) plus `select count(*) from urls;` trend before and after.

## 7. Escalation checklist

1. Confirm which surface is failing (read vs write vs both) using the status-mix dashboard.
2. Check readiness on the affected instances; if DOWN, treat as a Postgres incident.
3. Grep logs for `falling back to db_sequence` and `cache degradation` to classify a Redis incident.
4. If 5xx > 0.1%, capture a problem+json sample (it contains no secrets) and the correlating log window.
5. If code collisions (unexpected 409 on generated codes) appear, stop write instances immediately and re-seed the counter before restarting.
